messages:
anya: Heads-up — sampleapp CI failed after the latest typegen run on main. Regen produced a bunch of ordering changes and auth param shapes changed.
anya: CI job: https://ci.company/blue/1234
anya: Failed tests show signature mismatch when calling client.auth.retry()
ci-bot: build #1234 failed: unit tests (sampleapp) — see logs
sam: Ugh. Which PR caused the regen? any commit id?
anya: It looks like the change from PR #2491 where we reworked optional auth params (removed `opts.refresh` vs `opts.retry`) — typegen now reorders union types.
lina: That PR also bumped the typegen toolchain (typegen@2.8.0 -> 2.9.0). There was a hidden normalization fix that sorts properties differently.
michael: So the type hashes changed -> semver/packaging thinks it's a breaking change?
anya: Exactly. Local dev run: `npm run regen-types -- --spec openapi.yaml` produced diffs, then sampleapp compile errors.
anya: Snippet from failing TS error:
```
error TS2345: Argument of type '{ retry?: boolean; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'AuthOptions'.
  Property 'refresh' is missing in type '{ retry?: boolean; }' but required in type 'AuthOptions'.
```
sam: Could be that typegen now emits `refresh` required in some union branch due to ordering. If we don't want a breaking change we need to pin emitted shape or add a compatibility layer.
lina: Quick idea: add a CI gate that runs `yarn typegen:check` and fails if regenerated output differs from committed artifacts. We have a `devex-bot` action that can auto-post regen diffs.
devex-bot: Suggestion: enable `typegen:ci-check` step in sampleapp pipeline. Run `yarn typegen:check` and include `--tool-version 2.8.0` to force parity if needed.
michael: For short term fix: revert the typegen tool bump in the toolchain lockfile and re-run regen to restore previous ordering, then open a tracking issue for the new normalizing behavior.
anya: Revert seems fastest. But we should also decide long-term: accept new deterministic ordering (and make it a minor/major bump) vs maintain older nondeterministic output.
sam: We also need to ensure auth/retry behavior is not actually broken at runtime — this might just be a type mismatch. Can someone run a quick smoke test against staging?
lina: I ran a quick node script — runtime still accepts both shapes because runtime code checks for both keys. Types got stricter only.
anya: OK so runtime is fine. We should avoid a breaking semver bump accidentally. Proposal: revert tool bump on main, publish a patch to sampleapp types, and schedule a deprecation window when we intentionally adopt new shapes.
michael: I'll open the revert PR now and tag @lina for follow-up to add `typegen:check` in CI.
ci-bot: build #1236 triggered by michael/revert-typegen-toolchain
sam: Also add a tiny unit test that asserts the public SDK interface shape (so regen diffs can't quietly break consumers next time).
anya: Agreed. Quick checklist: revert tool bump, re-run regen, push commit; add CI check; add unit test; create tracking issue for typegen 2.9 behavior and planned semver migration.
michael: I'll handle revert + PR description explaining the rationale. ETA ~30m.
lina: I'll add the CI step in a follow-up PR and the unit test later today.
anya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
sam: thanks — ping me if anyone needs help debugging the regen command.
devex-bot: Note: filed issue DEVEX-812 for 'typegen output normalization and semver policy' and assigned to @lina and @michael.
anya: Sweet. Closing the loop here — will monitor CI and update thread.
